destinations.title: Dolphin Watching
destinations.subtitle: Wildlife & Boat Tours
destinations.overview: Kalpitiya is one of Sri Lanka’s best places to see large pods of spinner dolphins in the open sea. Early morning boat rides often bring close views of leaping dolphins, with chances of other marine life along the lagoon and ocean.
highlights: Morning boat safari from Kalpitiya lagoon
Calm lagoon scenery on the way out
destinations.tips: Wear light clothes, bring sunscreen, and start early for the best sea conditions.

destinations.title: Kite Surfing
destinations.subtitle: Adventure Seekers
destinations.overview: Steady winds and shallow lagoon waters make Kalpitiya a leading kite-surfing destination in Sri Lanka. Beginners can take lessons in sheltered water, while experienced riders head to the ocean side for stronger conditions.
destinations.tips: Book a certified instructor if you are new, and check daily wind conditions before heading out.

destinations.title: Dutch Fort
destinations.subtitle: History & Heritage
destinations.overview: The Kalpitiya Dutch Fort is a compact colonial stronghold that once guarded the lagoon entrance. Its thick coral walls and quiet courtyards give a glimpse of coastal defence history in the northwest.
destinations.tips: Combine the fort visit with a stroll through Kalpitiya town and a lagoon sunset.

destinations.title: 8 Sacred Places
destinations.subtitle: Culture & Pilgrimage
destinations.overview: Anuradhapura’s eight sacred sites, known as Atamasthana, form the spiritual heart of Sri Lanka’s ancient capital. Stupas, monastic ruins, and the sacred Bodhi tree create a full day of heritage and pilgrimage.
highlights: Sri Maha Bodhi and great stupas
destinations.tips: Dress modestly for temple visits and carry water, as walking between sites takes time.

destinations.title: Wilpattu Safari
destinations.subtitle: Wildlife Enthusiasts
destinations.overview: Wilpattu National Park is famous for natural lakes, or villus, and for leopard sightings in dry-zone forest. A jeep safari through this quieter park feels wilder and less crowded than many southern parks.
destinations.tips: Morning safaris are cooler and often better for wildlife. Carry binoculars if you have them.

destinations.title: Koneshwaram Temple
destinations.subtitle: Culture & Heritage
destinations.overview: Koneshwaram Temple sits on Swami Rock above Trincomalee harbour. The clifftop shrine, ocean views, and nearby historic spots make it one of the east coast’s most striking religious sites.
destinations.tips: Remove shoes before entering the shrine and visit in the morning or late afternoon for softer light.

destinations.title: Nilaveli Beach
destinations.subtitle: Beach Lovers
destinations.overview: Nilaveli is a long, pale beach north of Trincomalee, known for calm water, space, and a relaxed east-coast atmosphere. It is a good base for swimming, beach walks, and boat trips to nearby islands.
highlights: Easy access to island boat trips
destinations.tips: The east coast is best from roughly April to September, when seas are usually calmer.

destinations.title: Marble Beach
destinations.subtitle: Beach Lovers
destinations.overview: Marble Beach is a sheltered cove with clear, pale-blue water and a quieter feel than busier town beaches. It is popular for swimming, photos, and a slow afternoon by the sea.
destinations.tips: Arrive earlier in the day for a quieter shoreline and better parking.

destinations.title: Unuwathura Lin
destinations.subtitle: Nature & Island Tours
destinations.overview: Unuwathura Lin is a coastal nature stop near Trincomalee, often combined with beach and island time. The surrounding sea, rocks, and quiet shoreline suit a short boat or coastal visit.
destinations.tips: Ask your guide about sea conditions before booking a boat, especially outside the main season.

destinations.title: Whale Watching
destinations.subtitle: Wildlife & Boat Tours
destinations.overview: Trincomalee is a strong east-coast whale-watching base, with blue whales and sperm whales often seen offshore in season. Boat trips usually leave in the morning from the harbour area.
destinations.tips: Choose a responsible operator, take seasickness tablets if needed, and keep expectations flexible as sightings are never guaranteed.

destinations.title: Nallur Kovil
destinations.subtitle: Culture & Heritage
destinations.bestTime: July to August festival season, year-round visits
destinations.overview: Nallur Kandaswamy Kovil is Jaffna’s most famous Hindu temple, known for its golden towers, courtyards, and living worship traditions. The annual festival draws huge crowds and is one of the north’s great cultural events.
destinations.tips: Dress conservatively. Men may be asked to remove shirts inside the inner shrine.

destinations.title: Fort
destinations.subtitle: History & Heritage
destinations.overview: Jaffna Fort is a large star-shaped colonial fortress beside the lagoon. Walking the walls gives wide views over the water, old town, and layers of Portuguese, Dutch, and British history.
destinations.tips: Go late afternoon for cooler weather and sunset light on the lagoon.

destinations.title: Pinnawala
destinations.subtitle: Wildlife Enthusiasts
destinations.overview: Pinnawala is a well-known elephant orphanage stop on the way to Kandy. Visitors can watch feeding times and the herd walking to the river, making it a popular family-friendly wildlife experience.
highlights: Easy stop between Colombo and Kandy
destinations.tips: Time your visit with feeding or bathing hours. Choose ethical viewing spots and avoid crowding the animals.

destinations.title: Spice Garden
destinations.subtitle: Nature & Culture
destinations.overview: Hill-country spice gardens around Kandy grow cinnamon, pepper, cardamom, and Ayurvedic plants. A short guided walk explains how spices are grown and used in Sri Lankan cooking and traditional medicine.
destinations.tips: Buying is optional. Ask questions and compare prices if you do want spices or oils.

destinations.title: Gem Museum / Wood Carving
destinations.subtitle: Shopping & Crafts
destinations.overview: Kandy’s craft stops include gem displays and traditional wood carving workshops. They are a practical way to see local materials, cutting, and carving techniques before browsing finished pieces.
destinations.tips: Ask for certificates on gem purchases and take time rather than buying on the first stop.

destinations.title: Tooth Temple
destinations.subtitle: Culture & Heritage
destinations.bestTime: Year-round; Esala Perahera season is especially memorable
destinations.overview: The Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic is Kandy’s most important Buddhist shrine and a UNESCO World Heritage site. Evening puja, drumming, and lakeside setting make it a highlight of any cultural tour.
destinations.tips: Cover shoulders and knees, and allow extra time during puja hours when crowds are larger.

destinations.title: Cultural Dance
destinations.subtitle: Culture & Performances
destinations.overview: Kandyan dance performances bring drums, costumes, and fire acts from the hill-country tradition. A theatre show is an easy evening add-on after temple and city visits.
destinations.tips: Book seats closer to the stage for better photos, and arrive a little early.

destinations.title: Mahamevnawa Monastery
destinations.subtitle: Culture & Pilgrimage
destinations.overview: Mahamevnawa Monastery near Kandy is a calm Buddhist centre known for its serene grounds and teaching tradition. It offers a quieter spiritual stop compared with the busy lakeside temple.
destinations.tips: Keep voices low, dress modestly, and check visiting hours before you go.

destinations.title: Peradeniya Garden
destinations.subtitle: Nature Lovers
destinations.overview: The Royal Botanical Gardens at Peradeniya are among Asia’s finest tropical gardens, with orchid houses, giant trees, and landscaped avenues beside the Mahaweli River.
highlights: Orchid house and giant fig trees
destinations.tips: Wear comfortable shoes; the gardens are large and best enjoyed at an unhurried pace.

destinations.title: Tea Factory
destinations.subtitle: Scenic & Culture
destinations.overview: A tea factory visit in Nuwara Eliya shows how Ceylon tea is plucked, withered, rolled, and tasted. Estate views and a cup of freshly brewed tea complete the hill-country experience.
destinations.tips: Bring a light jacket; factory floors and estate viewpoints can be cool.

destinations.title: Ramboda Falls
destinations.subtitle: Nature Lovers
destinations.bestTime: After rains, with care on wet paths
destinations.overview: Ramboda Falls drops in a tall white cascade beside the Kandy–Nuwara Eliya road. It is a popular photo stop with viewpoints above and below the waterfall.
destinations.tips: Watch your footing on spray-wet steps and avoid standing too close to the edge.

destinations.title: Post Office
destinations.subtitle: History & Heritage
destinations.overview: The red-brick Nuwara Eliya Post Office is a colonial landmark in the town centre. It is a quick heritage photo stop that captures the hill station’s British-era character.
destinations.tips: Visit in daylight for the best photos, then continue to the lake or nearby parks.

destinations.title: Gregory Lake
destinations.subtitle: Families & Couples
destinations.overview: Gregory Lake is Nuwara Eliya’s easygoing waterside promenade, with boat rides, swan pedals, and mountain views. It is a relaxed stop for families, couples, and evening walks.
destinations.tips: Late afternoon is pleasant for photos, but it can get busy on weekends.

destinations.title: Horton Plains
destinations.subtitle: Hiking & Nature
destinations.bestTime: December to April for clearer views
destinations.overview: Horton Plains National Park is a high-altitude grassland and cloud-forest hike to World’s End and Baker’s Falls. Early starts are rewarded with the best chance of a clear cliff-edge view.
destinations.tips: Enter early, wear layers, and keep to marked paths. Mist can hide the view later in the morning.

destinations.title: Sandathanna Safari
destinations.subtitle: Wildlife Enthusiasts
destinations.bestTime: Year-round, clearer in the dry months
destinations.overview: Sandathanna Safari is a hill-country wildlife drive near Nuwara Eliya, offering a quieter alternative to the large national parks. Expect forest scenery, birds, and a chance of sambar and other highland animals.
destinations.tips: Carry a jacket and ask the tracker which gate and time give the best recent sightings.

destinations.title: Hakgala / Victoria Park
destinations.subtitle: Nature Lovers
destinations.bestTime: April flower season and cool dry months
destinations.overview: Hakgala Botanical Garden and Victoria Park are two of Nuwara Eliya’s greenest spaces. Rose beds, temperate plants, and shaded paths make them a gentle contrast to long hill drives.
destinations.tips: These are easy town-side visits, ideal if you want scenery without a long hike.

destinations.title: Ambewela Farm
destinations.subtitle: Families
destinations.overview: Ambewela Farm sits in open highland pasture and is known for dairy views, cool air, and family-friendly farm stops. It is a scenic add-on between Nuwara Eliya and Horton Plains.
destinations.tips: The area is often windy and cooler than town, so keep a warm layer handy.

destinations.title: Helicopter Tour
destinations.subtitle: Adventure Seekers
destinations.overview: A helicopter tour over Nuwara Eliya reveals tea estates, peaks, and valleys from the air. It is a premium add-on for guests who want a fast, dramatic view of the hill country.
destinations.tips: Flights depend on weather. Keep the schedule flexible and confirm the briefing time the day before.

destinations.title: Train Tour
destinations.subtitle: Scenic Journeys
destinations.bestTime: January to April for clearer views
destinations.overview: The train through tea country to Ella is one of Sri Lanka’s most famous journeys. Carriages pass tea terraces, villages, and misty hills, with the Nine Arch Bridge as a landmark along the way.
highlights: Kandy or Nanu Oya to Ella rail journey
destinations.tips: Reserve seats in advance when possible. The right-side window is often preferred on the way to Ella.

destinations.title: Nine Arch Bridge
destinations.subtitle: Scenic & Photography
destinations.bestTime: Year-round; check train times for photos
destinations.overview: Nine Arch Bridge is Ella’s signature colonial viaduct, curving through jungle and tea slopes. Visitors walk down from town for viewpoints and wait for the train to cross.
destinations.tips: Check the train timetable and stay well off the tracks when a train approaches.

destinations.title: Little Adams Peak
destinations.subtitle: Hiking & Nature
destinations.overview: Little Adams Peak is a short, rewarding hike above Ella with wide views over tea estates and Ella Rock. The climb is moderate and popular at sunrise.
destinations.tips: Wear shoes with grip. Paths can be slippery after rain.

destinations.title: Rawana Falls
destinations.subtitle: Nature Lovers
destinations.overview: Rawana Falls is a broad roadside waterfall below Ella, linked in legend to the Ramayana. It is an easy photo stop, with a short walk toward the cascade if conditions are safe.
destinations.tips: Rocks are slippery. Keep a safe distance from fast water.

destinations.title: Galle Dutch Fort
destinations.subtitle: History & Heritage
destinations.overview: Galle Fort is a living UNESCO World Heritage town of ramparts, lighthouses, cafes, and colonial streets. Sunset on the walls is one of the south coast’s classic moments.
destinations.tips: Explore on foot. Late afternoon is cooler and best for wall-top photos.

destinations.title: Whale Watching Mirissa
destinations.subtitle: Wildlife & Boat Tours
destinations.overview: Mirissa is the south coast’s main whale-watching harbour, with seasonal blue whale sightings not far offshore. Boats typically leave at dawn and return before noon.
highlights: Blue whale season on the south coast
destinations.tips: Pick a responsible operator that limits crowding around whales, and eat lightly before boarding.

destinations.title: Unawatuna Beach
destinations.subtitle: Beach Lovers
destinations.overview: Unawatuna is a curved bay near Galle with swimming, beach restaurants, and an easy-going south-coast mood. It is convenient after a Fort visit or as a longer beach stay.
destinations.tips: The bay is busier at weekends. For a quieter swim, go earlier in the day.

destinations.title: Coconut Tree Hill
destinations.subtitle: Scenic & Photography
destinations.overview: Coconut Tree Hill in Mirissa is a small headland of leaning palms above the sea, famous for photographs. The walk is short and pairs well with beach time.
destinations.tips: Go early to avoid crowds and strong midday sun.

destinations.title: Turtle Hatchery and Beach Hikkaduwa
destinations.subtitle: Wildlife & Beaches
destinations.overview: Hikkaduwa combines a lively beach with nearby turtle hatcheries that protect eggs and release hatchlings. It is a south-coast stop that mixes swimming, snorkelling, and conservation visits.
destinations.tips: Choose hatcheries with a clear conservation focus and follow staff guidance around nesting areas.

destinations.title: Moonstone Shop
destinations.subtitle: Shopping & Crafts
destinations.overview: Moonstone workshops near the south-west coast show how Sri Lanka’s milky-blue gem is mined, cut, and set. It is a short craft stop often included on Galle-area tours.
destinations.tips: Buying is optional. Compare quality and ask questions before making a purchase.

destinations.title: Madu River
destinations.subtitle: Nature & Boat Tours
destinations.overview: A Madu River boat ride glides through mangroves, small islands, and cinnamon-growing waterways near Balapitiya. Fish therapy stops and island temples are common extras.
destinations.tips: Morning trips are cooler and often better for birds.

destinations.title: Water Sports in Bentota
destinations.subtitle: Adventure Seekers
destinations.overview: Bentota is Sri Lanka’s classic water-sports bay, with jet skiing, banana boats, diving, and lagoon activities. It is an easy adventure stop on the south-west coast.
highlights: Jet ski and banana boat options
destinations.tips: Use licensed operators and life jackets, and confirm what is included before you start.

destinations.title: Yala Safari
destinations.subtitle: Wildlife Enthusiasts
destinations.overview: Yala National Park is Sri Lanka’s best-known safari park, with leopards, elephants, crocodiles, and coastal lagoons. It is often combined with south-coast itineraries from the Galle side.
destinations.tips: Morning game drives are usually more productive. Carry water, a hat, and a dust scarf.

destinations.title: Kataragama Kovil
destinations.subtitle: Culture & Pilgrimage
destinations.bestTime: Year-round; festival season is especially busy
destinations.overview: Kataragama is a shared sacred town where Hindu, Buddhist, and other traditions meet. The evening puja at the main shrine is atmospheric, with lamps, drums, and pilgrims.
destinations.tips: Dress modestly and keep photography respectful around active rituals.

destinations.title: Mask Museum Ambalangoda
destinations.subtitle: Culture & Heritage
destinations.overview: Ambalangoda is the home of Sri Lankan ritual dance masks. The museum and nearby workshops explain kolam, devil dance, and carving traditions of the south-west coast.
destinations.tips: A short stop is enough for the museum; add a workshop visit if you want to see carving in progress.

destinations.title: Gangaramaya Temple
destinations.subtitle: Culture & Heritage
destinations.overview: Gangaramaya is one of Colombo’s most visited temples, mixing shrines, a museum-like collection, and a lakeside setting at Beira Lake. It is a compact introduction to the city’s Buddhist life.
destinations.tips: Remove shoes and hats, and allow time to wander the inner courtyards.

destinations.title: Independence Square
destinations.subtitle: History & City Walks
destinations.bestTime: Year-round, cooler in the morning or evening
destinations.overview: Independence Square commemorates Sri Lanka’s independence with a grand memorial hall and open lawns. It is a popular walking and photo stop in Colombo 7.
destinations.tips: Combine with nearby Arcade Independence Square if you want cafes after the monument.

destinations.title: Colombo Fort
destinations.subtitle: History & Heritage
destinations.overview: Colombo Fort is the old commercial heart of the city, with colonial buildings, clock towers, and busy streets leading toward the harbour and Pettah. It is best seen on a guided city walk.
destinations.tips: Go with a driver or guide in peak traffic, and keep valuables close in crowded streets.

destinations.title: Galle Face Green
destinations.subtitle: City & Seaside
destinations.overview: Galle Face Green is Colombo’s oceanfront promenade, where families fly kites, eat street snacks, and watch the sunset over the Indian Ocean.
destinations.tips: Sunset is the liveliest time. Bring cash for snacks and a light layer if the sea breeze picks up.

destinations.title: Red Mosque of Pettah
destinations.subtitle: Culture & Heritage
destinations.bestTime: Year-round, outside prayer peak if you want a quieter visit
destinations.overview: The Red Mosque, or Jami Ul-Alfar, is Pettah’s candy-striped landmark. Its red-and-white facade is one of Colombo’s most photographed buildings.
destinations.tips: Dress modestly. Interior access can be limited around prayer times.

destinations.title: Hindu Temple
destinations.subtitle: Culture & Heritage
destinations.overview: Colombo’s Hindu temples, including well-known kovils in the city, add colour, sculpture, and ritual to a city tour. Gopurams, incense, and evening puja make a strong cultural stop.
destinations.tips: Remove footwear, dress conservatively, and ask before photographing inner shrines.

destinations.title: Lion Rock (Sigiriya)
destinations.subtitle: History & Hiking
destinations.overview: Sigiriya, the Lion Rock, is a 5th-century palace-fortress rising from the jungle. The climb passes frescoes, the Mirror Wall, and lion’s-paw terraces before a summit with 360-degree views.
destinations.tips: Start early to beat heat and crowds. Wear shoes with grip and carry water.

destinations.title: Cave Temple
destinations.subtitle: Culture & Heritage
destinations.overview: Dambulla Cave Temple is a UNESCO rock monastery with five cave shrines filled with Buddha images and painted ceilings. It is a core stop in the Cultural Triangle.
destinations.tips: The climb is short but steep and can be hot. Barefoot temple rules apply inside the caves.

destinations.title: Village Tour
destinations.subtitle: Local Experiences
destinations.overview: A village tour around Dambulla introduces rural life in the Cultural Triangle: bullock carts, catamaran lake crossings, cookery, and garden walks. It balances the big heritage sites with local hospitality.
destinations.tips: This is a slower experience. Go with an open schedule and comfortable clothes.

destinations.title: Hurulu Eco Park Safari Minneriya
destinations.subtitle: Wildlife Enthusiasts
destinations.bestTime: July to October for the Gathering, other months still good
destinations.overview: Hurulu Eco Park and nearby Minneriya are known for elephant herds gathering around reservoirs. A jeep safari here is one of the best dry-zone wildlife experiences near Dambulla.
destinations.tips: Afternoon safaris can be excellent around water. Confirm which park is open and best on your date.

destinations.title: Hot Air Balloon Ride
destinations.subtitle: Adventure Seekers
destinations.overview: A hot-air balloon ride over the Cultural Triangle offers sunrise views of Sigiriya, forest, and village tanks. Flights are weather-dependent and usually start before dawn.
highlights: Champagne-style landing experience on many tours
destinations.tips: Expect an early pickup. Flights can be postponed if the wind is not right.

destinations.title: Arugam Bay Surf
destinations.subtitle: Surf & Beach Lovers
destinations.overview: Arugam Bay is Sri Lanka’s best-known surf town, with a right-hand point break and a laid-back east-coast village. It suits surfers of mixed levels as well as guests who just want beach time.
destinations.tips: Peak swell is on the east-coast season. Book lessons in the morning when crowds and wind are usually kinder.
